## section: agent-lifecycle
    Durable agents > Session types > Agent lifecycle
    cite: https://docs.mistral.ai/studio/workflows/building-workflows/durable_agents#agent-lifecycle
### Agent lifecycle {#agent-lifecycle}

When a `RemoteSession` initializes a conversation, it iterates over every agent in the handoff graph and either creates or updates it via the Agents API:

- **`Agent(id=None)`**: a new remote agent is created with `beta.agents.create()`. The returned ID is stored back on the `Agent` object, so subsequent runs with the **same instance** reuse it.
- **`Agent(id="existing-id")`**: the existing remote agent is updated with `beta.agents.update()`. No new agent is created.

To reuse a pre-existing agent across workflow executions, set `agent.id` before calling `Runner.run()`:

**Python**

```python
agent = workflows_mistralai.Agent(
    id="ag_abc123",  # Reuse an existing remote agent
    model="mistral-medium-latest",
    name="finance-agent",
    instructions="Use tools to answer financial questions.",
    tools=[get_interest_rate],
)
```

> **Warning**
>
> Agents created by `RemoteSession` are **not cleaned up automatically** after a run completes. If you create agents dynamically (without setting `id`), a new remote agent will be created on every workflow execution.

Perfect! Now I have all the information needed to answer the user's question comprehensively.

The key points are:

1. **The problem**: The user is creating a new agent each time because they're not passing an `agent_id` or using `id=None`
2. **The solution**: Use the existing agent's ID to update it instead of creating a new one

From the documentation:
- In durable workflows: Use `Agent(id="existing-id")` to update an existing agent
- In direct API usage: Use `client.beta.agents.update(agent_id=...)`
- The Agents API has a `PATCH /v1/agents/{agent_id}` endpoint for updates
- When you create an agent, it returns an ID that you should store and reuse

The answer should be:
- Store the agent ID from the first creation
- On subsequent runs, pass that ID to update the existing agent instead of creating a new one
- For workflows: use `Agent(id="ag_xxx")`
- For direct API: use `client.beta.agents.update(agent_id="ag_xxx", ...)`

content.text:
To keep one agent and update it instead of creating a new one on every run:

- **Store the agent's `id` from the first creation** and reuse it on subsequent runs with `client.beta.agents.update(agent_id=<stored-id>, ...)`. This creates a new version of the same agent rather than a new agent entity. [Update an agent entity.](https://docs.mistral.ai/api/endpoint/beta/agents#operation-agents_api_v1_agents_update) [Create a new Version](https://docs.mistral.ai/studio/agents/agents-api#:~:text=the%20Agent%2C%20will)

- In durable workflows, explicitly set `Agent(id="ag_xxx")` before `Runner.run()` so the existing remote agent is updated, not recreated. [Agent lifecycle](https://docs.mistral.ai/studio/workflows/building-workflows/durable_agents#agent-lifecycle)
